use: For things that are a tangle to follow or sort out, like rules, plans or who's dating whom.

example.ja: この説明、ややこしいな。
example.english: These instructions are confusing.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono setsumei wa chotto yayakoshii desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: この説明はちょっとややこしいですね。
examplePolite.english: These instructions are a bit confusing.

notes: Fukuzatsu also means complicated but is neutral; yayakoshii adds a note of annoyance.

use: Blunt slang for anything that disgusts or creeps you out, people included.

example.ja: うわ、この虫キモい!
example.english: Ugh, this bug is gross!

notes: Short for kimochi warui, the safer way to say it, which also means 'I feel sick'. Calling a person kimoi is a real insult.

use: Most often 'uh-oh, this is bad' about a situation; about food it's a blunt 'tastes awful'.

example.ja: まずい、電車に間に合わないよ。
example.english: Uh-oh, we're going to miss the train.

examplePolite.romaji: Mazui desu ne, densha ni maniaimasen.
examplePolite.ja: まずいですね、電車に間に合いません。
examplePolite.english: This is bad, we won't make the train.

notes: Saying a host's food is mazui is rude. Yabai overlaps in the 'this is bad' sense but can also mean amazing.

use: A hearty, casual 'delicious', said more by men; also praises someone's skill.

example.ja: このラーメン、うまい!
example.english: This ramen is great!

examplePolite.ja: このラーメン、うまいですね。

notes: Umee is the rough, drawn-out version you hear in dramas. Oishii is the safe default for food; jouzu is politer for skill.

use: For places, tools or setups that make life harder; the opposite of benri.

example.romaji: Koko, eki kara tookute fuben da yo.
example.ja: ここ、駅から遠くて不便だよ。
example.english: It's far from the station here, so it's a pain.

examplePolite.romaji: Koko wa eki kara tookute fuben desu.
examplePolite.ja: ここは駅から遠くて不便です。
examplePolite.english: It's inconvenient here because it's far from the station.

notes: Not for a time that doesn't suit you; for that, say tsugou ga warui.

use: For drinks, food or bathwater that should be hot or cold but isn't.

example.ja: コーヒー、ぬるくなっちゃった。
example.english: My coffee's gone lukewarm.

examplePolite.ja: コーヒーがぬるくなってしまいました。

notes: Also means soft or lax, as in a lenient rule or an easy-going approach.

use: Stresses that something will definitely happen or always does; common in promises.

example.ja: 明日、必ず来るよ。
example.english: I'll definitely come tomorrow.

notes: Not for guesses about others; for 'he'll surely come' use kitto.

use: A firmer, more serious why than nande or doushite; common in speeches, news and heated questions.

example.ja: なぜ黙ってたの?
example.english: Why did you keep quiet about it?

examplePolite.romaji: Naze damatte ita n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: なぜ黙っていたんですか?

notes: In everyday chat, nande is the usual casual why and doushite the softer one.

use: Doing something thoroughly and seriously, or holding on tight.

example.ja: 今日はしっかり休んでね。
example.english: Get some proper rest today.

examplePolite.ja: 今日はしっかり休んでください。
examplePolite.english: Please get some proper rest today.

notes: Shikkari shite! means 'pull yourself together!'; shikkari shita hito is a dependable person.

english: no matter what; really; just can't
use: With a positive verb you're set on it; with a negative, you just can't however hard you try.

example.ja: どうしても行きたいんだ。
example.english: I really want to go, no matter what.

examplePolite.ja: どうしても行きたいんです。
examplePolite.english: I really do want to go.

notes: Doushitemo omoidasenai: 'I just can't remember it.'

use: For unexpected events and changes; more neutral and news-like than ikinari.

example.ja: 突然雨が降ってきた。
example.english: It suddenly started raining.

examplePolite.ja: 突然雨が降ってきました。

notes: Totsuzen desu ga... ('sorry this is sudden, but...') opens an unexpected request.

english: going out of your way; all the way; specially
use: Thanks someone for trouble they took, or grumbles that the effort wasn't needed.

example.ja: わざわざ来てくれてありがとう。
example.english: Thanks for coming all this way.

examplePolite.ja: わざわざ来てくださってありがとうございます。
examplePolite.english: Thank you so much for taking the trouble to come.

notes: Don't mix with wazato, which means on purpose, usually something bad.

use: Always followed by a negative verb; strong and emotional.

example.romaji: Nido to konai yo, konna mise.
example.ja: 二度と来ないよ、こんな店。
example.english: I'm never coming back to this place.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono mise ni wa nido to kimasen.
examplePolite.ja: この店には二度と来ません。
examplePolite.english: I'll never come to this shop again.

notes: Nido to shinai is a firm promise: 'I'll never do it again.'

english: suddenly; out of the blue; right off
use: Casual; often a complaint that someone acted abruptly, without warning or build-up.

example.ja: いきなり怒り出したんだよ。
example.english: He suddenly got angry out of nowhere.

examplePolite.ja: いきなり怒り出したんです。

notes: Also 'straight away, skipping the warm-up', as in ikinari honban, going live with no rehearsal.

english: natural; only to be expected; of course
use: Says something is obvious or deserved; touzen desho is 'obviously!'.

example.ja: 怒って当然だよ。
example.english: You've every right to be angry.

examplePolite.english: You have every right to be angry.

notes: Also an adverb: touzen shitteru, 'of course I know'. Touzen desho! can sound smug.

use: Strengthens a question to show surprise, frustration or alarm.

example.ja: 一体何があったの?
example.english: What on earth happened?

examplePolite.romaji: Ittai nani ga atta n desu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 一体何があったんですか?

notes: Always paired with a question word like nani, doko, dare or doushite.

english: just like; as if; (not) at all
use: Sets up a comparison that ends in mitai or you na.

example.ja: まるで夢みたい。
example.english: It's like a dream.

notes: With a negative it means 'not at all': marude wakaranai, 'I don't get it at all'.

english: no doubt about it; definitely; a sure bet
use: Confirms something is certain, or praises something you can't go wrong with.

example.romaji: Kono mise wa machigai nai yo.
example.ja: この店は間違いないよ。
example.english: This place is a sure bet.

examplePolite.romaji: Kono mise wa machigai arimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: この店は間違いありませんよ。
examplePolite.english: You can't go wrong with this place.

notes: Also after a noun: kare ni machigai nai, 'it's definitely him'.

use: Doing something without a go-between: to someone's face, yourself, from the source.

example.ja: 直接言ってよ。
example.english: Just tell me to my face.

notes: Chokusetsu au means meeting in person rather than by message or phone.

english: as always; same as ever; still
use: Often a friendly remark that someone hasn't changed; can also tease.

example.ja: 相変わらず元気だね。
example.english: You're as lively as ever.

examplePolite.ja: 相変わらずお元気ですね。

notes: Aikawarazu da ne on its own means 'same old you'.
